description: Sabotages for measure-sweep-durations.ps1, the script the durable-ioring manifests' timeoutSeconds is measured with, judged by test-measure-sweep-durations.ps1. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1 -Manifest tools/sabotage-sweep-durations.json -CargoCommand tools/sabotage-sweep-durations-runner.cmd; see tools/README-sabotage.md.

sabotages.name: a build launch is counted as a suite
sabotages.why: A build takes several times as long as the suite on these runners, so counting it would raise every percentile the bound is set from.

sabotages.name: a narrowed run that caught the entry is counted as a suite
sabotages.why: A narrowed run is a few tests, so counting it would pull the entry durations down to a few seconds and say nothing about the suite.

sabotages.name: the first run launch of an entry is taken instead of the last
sabotages.why: After a narrowed run that was not credited, the suite runs second; taking the first records the narrowed run's duration as the suite's.

sabotages.name: a launch killed at the bound is dropped
sabotages.why: The killed launches are the evidence that a bound is inside the tail; dropping them reports a sweep that has none.
find: if ($line -match 'the bound of (\d+)ms was reached') { $pending = @{ Code = 'bound'; Ms = [int]$Matches[1] }; continue }
replace: if ($line -match 'the bound of (\d+)ms was reached') { continue }

sabotages.name: the percentile rounds its rank down
sabotages.why: Nearest rank is the ceiling of p x n; flooring it reports the sample below, which for p99.9 of 1,000 is the 998th.

sabotages.name: a log for another manifest is read
sabotages.why: Every manifest's shard logs share the cache directory, so a manifest asked about would take on another's durations.

sabotages.name: control: the verdict's trailing timing is stripped with a looser pattern
sabotages.why: A control. The harness always ends a verdict with '(Ns)' or '(Ns, ~... left)', which both patterns remove, so no row changes.
